question: In the connective tissues of animals, the fat cells are arranged into lobules, which are separated by partitions of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**collagen and elastin fibres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Fat cells**, also known as **adipocytes**, are primarily found in connective tissues, which serve as the structural framework for tissues and organs in animals.
 
• In connective tissue, fat cells are organized into **lobules**, or clusters, which are separated by partitions made of **collagen and elastin fibres.**
 
• **Collagen fibres** provide strength and structural support to the tissue, while **elastin fibres** contribute elasticity, allowing the tissue to stretch and return to its original shape.
 
• The combination of collagen and elastin ensures the connective tissue is both strong and flexible, enabling it to withstand mechanical forces and maintain the integrity of the fat lobules.
